findings.breaking_input: Two tabs are open. Tab B folds the first ring, so storage holds that ring as false. Tab A still shows it open, because its in-memory `saved` has no entry and the default for the first ring is open. The viewer clicks the header in tab A to fold it. onToggle merges storage over `saved` into `fresh` and calls toggleRing on `fresh`. `fresh` says the ring is folded, so toggleRing writes true. Tab A re-renders with the ring still open.
findings.why: The decision is made on one read (storage) while the screen shows another (the tab's `saved`). The click looks dead and the stored value is flipped to the state already on screen. This is the fix for attack 0991e16 B1, and the fix creates this case.
findings.fix: Merge storage into `saved` first with setSaved. Or compute the toggle from the state the viewer sees (`open[ring]`) and write only that ring's key over the fresh storage copy.
findings.twin_of: Viewer state written to storage on mount, from a stale in-memory copy -> Check: per-viewer storage is written only on the viewer's own act, merged over what storage holds at that moment.

findings.breaking_input: Open the drawer for a humanRun, leavesMachine or spends op (daily mail send, bench run) and click Apply. While the request is in flight, press Esc, click ×, or click another strip item. The drawer unmounts (or remounts via key=openKey) and the OpCardView state goes back to idle. The viewer reopens it, re-plans and applies again.
findings.why: A window-level Esc closes the drawer even while a form is mid-call. The in-flight answer lands on an unmounted card, so the receipt and the sent/spent state are lost. A mail op has no server-side in-flight slot, so a second send is invited. Nothing blocks closing while busy, which is the pattern of a form cleared before the server answered.
findings.fix: Have the card report busy. Ignore Esc, × and item switches while an op or session start is in flight. Or keep the card state above the drawer so the answer survives a close.
findings.twin_of: A form cleared before the server answered -> Check: an edit form closes on the server's acceptance, never on submit.

findings.breaking_input: If useAsk returns a `close` that is a fresh function each render (not useCallback), every render re-runs the effect. Asking a question sets state and re-renders, the effect calls close(), and the answer card shuts as it appears.
findings.why: The effect depends on the function's identity, but the intent is to run only when `place` changes. It also runs close() on mount.
findings.fix: Run the effect on `[place]` only, keeping `close` in a ref. Or memoize `close` in useAsk and pin that with a test that asks, then re-renders without changing place, and expects the answer to stay.

findings.where: face/src/shell/RoomFrame.tsx: registry useEffect with deps [door, m]
findings.breaking_input: Any parent re-render that gives ModuleView a new `m` object for the same room, such as an attachment recompute or a registry re-read. The effect aborts, sets both registries to null, and re-fetches. While they are null, `strip` is empty, `sessionCount` is 0 and `tabs` is ['overview']. currentTab drops the viewer from Work to Overview, and `openItem` is undefined so the open drawer disappears with its half-typed form.
findings.why: Tab and drawer state is derived from async registries that are blanked on identity churn rather than on a room change. Keying on the object `m` instead of `m.id` turns a re-render into a visible state reset.
findings.fix: Key the effect on `m.id` and `door`. Keep the last good registries while a re-read is in flight, and null them only when the room id changes.
findings.twin_of: A failed re-read replacing a good answer -> Check: a re-read that fails keeps the last good answer and says so.

findings.where: face/src/shell/RoomFrame.tsx (Work tab OpsDock/SessionDock plus drawer OpsDock/SessionDock) and face/scripts/flows.mjs:dockState
findings.breaking_input: On the Work tab, open a strip item. The same op card (`data-op=<id>`) and the same `data-session-dock=<room>` now exist twice in one section, one in `[data-frame-work]` and one in the drawer. dockState's `section[data-room] [data-session-dock]` returns whichever comes first in the DOM, the Work tab copy. A Start clicked in the drawer is read through the other dock.
findings.why: Two live instances of one card hold independent state. The harness selector was scoped for the op card (`[data-frame-work]`) but not for the session dock, so one selector query can read a different element than the one acted on.
findings.fix: Do not render the Work-tab copy of a card while its drawer is open. Or scope every harness selector to either `[data-frame-work]` or `[data-action-drawer]`.
findings.twin_of: A pick and a click in one synchronous script -> Check: a positive control must be deterministic on every runner.

findings.breaking_input: /api/bench returns two run rows with the same `id`. Both rows get `key: id`, so React sees duplicate keys and `data-served-row` collides. With the 8-row cap and the "show all" toggle, one duplicate row can hide or replace its twin on reorder.
findings.why: The rows are not deduplicated or counted when ids repeat. Elsewhere the lane already had to fix a name the registry listed twice being drawn under a duplicate key.
findings.fix: Include the row index in the key. Better, drop repeated ids in the row builder and count them as `duplicates`.
findings.twin_of: A name the registry listed twice was counted twice and drawn under a duplicate React key -> Rows the fold cannot tell apart are counted, not drawn.

findings.breaking_input: A role served with `reports_to` set to a long or multi-line string, or an `id` outside the role-id grammar. It is printed raw into the Owner node's sub line, the chip `title` attribute, `data-org-chip` and the card's id line. Two roles with an empty `id` collide on byId key "", so a missing `reports_to` is counted as reporting to that role and it becomes the CEO.
findings.why: Ids and refs from the served body are drawn without a grammar check or a one-line cap, and byId accepts the empty id. This is an id served outside its grammar.
findings.fix: Skip any role whose id fails the role-id grammar, and count those. Run printed refs through the one-line and length cap before drawing.
findings.twin_of: A fold that echoes payload strings into labels -> Check: a ref printed from data matches its grammar or is not printed.
